sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Describe one trend in a chart you have seen recently. What does it suggest, and what does it not prove?
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Research presentations describe data precisely, interpret cautiously and acknowledge limits honestly.

blocks.text: Describe data before interpreting it. “Die Zahl der Teilnehmenden ist von 120 auf 180 gestiegen” is description. “Das legt nahe, dass die Maßnahme wirkt” is interpretation. Keeping the two separate lets the audience judge your conclusion.

Use precise trend language: “ein leichter Anstieg”, “ein deutlicher Rückgang”, “stagnieren”, “sich verdoppeln”. For interpretation, use “legen nahe”, “deuten auf … hin”, “lässt vermuten”. For limitations, name the sample, period, method or missing data.

blocks.title: Correlation is not causation
blocks.text: If two numbers move together, say “Es besteht ein Zusammenhang”. Do not say “A verursacht B” unless the design supports that claim.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Die Zahl ist von 120 auf 180 gestiegen.

items: “Steigen” and “sinken” are strong verbs; “leicht” and “deutlich” qualify them.
“Die Aussagekraft” means explanatory power or validity.
Name the time period for every trend: im Vergleich zum Vorjahr.

sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The d is soft at the end: trent.

blocks.text: German media often cite statistics from official sources such as Destatis. A good presentation names the source and the period, not just the number.
Percentages and percentage points are frequently confused. “Die Arbeitslosigkeit stieg um zwei Prozent” is different from “um zwei Prozentpunkte”.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Describing and interpreting data
sections.lede: Keep description, interpretation and limitation in separate sentences.

rows: Die Zahl ist von … auf … gestiegen.

blocks.text: Use “im Vergleich zu” for comparisons: Im Vergleich zum Vorjahr ist die Zahl um 15 Prozent gestiegen. Name the baseline, or the number means little.

sections.tip: For every chart, say three things: what changed, by how much, and over what period.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Describe a trend, interpret it cautiously and name one limitation.

model.de: Die Zahl der Teilnehmenden ist von 120 auf 180 gestiegen. Das legt nahe, dass die Kampagne bekannter geworden ist. Die Aussagekraft ist jedoch begrenzt, weil nur eine Stadt untersucht wurde.
model.en: The number of participants rose from 120 to 180. That suggests the campaign has become better known. However, the validity is limited because only one city was studied.

tips: Give the numbers and the period.
Name one concrete limitation, not a general caveat.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Die Zahl ist von 120 auf 180 gestiegen auf.
items.right: Die Zahl ist von 120 auf 180 gestiegen.
items.why: Steigen does not take a separable prefix here; auf belongs to the von … auf phrase.
The plural subject takes the plural verb legen.

items.wrong: Das beweist, dass die Kampagne wirkt.
items.right: Das legt nahe, dass die Kampagne wirkt.
items.why: A correlation does not prove causation.
